I was FOH - a waiter - and I miss it. I miss bullshitting in spanish with the chefs. I miss that awesome feeling of kicking the ass out of a rush. I miss bitching about cunty customers with the staff. I miss the good, the bad, and the ugly.

Working in a restaurant and hanging out in the kitchen with everyone was an awesome experience that I wouldn't trade for anything.
I miss working in a restaurant.

Couldn't agree more. I was a dishwasher. 12 years I was a dishwasher at different restaurants down the coast. I have a PhD and I'm in academic research now, but man, I still daydream about my dishwashing days. On those busiest nights, when stress levels were highest, we still knocked it out and gave everybody what they needed. While listening to horrible music on our boom box that was bungied to the shelf. And Poison's "Nothin' but a good time" was a big hit back then. I hate that I'd still trade it all to be back in that washroom again. Best job I ever had.

I'm currently a waitress at two places. 99% of customers are awesome but the other 1% can just ruin your day. But I love that feeling when you just finish a busy shift with little to no hitches. It's super rewarding! :)
I know that feeling man. I think if you really miss it, maybe open your own place.

While removing myself from the line was the best choice for me health-wise, I still miss it every single day (and it's been almost 20 years). In some ways it helps that my wife is still working FOH and I get to hear her war stories, but sometimes it makes me sad that I sit in an office 8-5 M-F. Don't get me wrong, weekends and holidays off, health insurance, and all of the other perks that come from a stable office job are great, and I cook huge dinners for friends and family very regularly, but I'll never forget the feeling of tightening my apron, hunkering down, and hammering out 500+ covers on a steamy summer night, or the taste of the ice cold beer afterwards. Beer and weed never tasted that good after I left the kitchen.
